look_here_first: Check alternate diamond-shaped leaves with a long tapering tip and nearly smooth margins; inspect the leaf-blade base for small glands. Then look for slender flower spikes or a 3-lobed capsule that opens to three bright white wax-coated seeds.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Deciduous tree with alternate, simple, broadly rhombic to triangular-ovate leaves

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Leaves often have an elongated pointed tip, smooth to nearly smooth margin, and long slender petiole

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Small glands near junction of petiole and leaf blade may be visible on close inspection

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Terminal yellow-green flower spikes with numerous small flowers

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Three-lobed/three-chambered capsules; opening fruit exposes three white waxy seeds resembling popcorn

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Autumn leaves can turn red or yellow, but color is not diagnostic

lookalikes.differences: Texas redbud has cordate leaves and pea-family pods rather than three-lobed capsules with white waxy seeds. Cottonwood/poplar seedlings have toothed triangular leaves and cottony seeds rather than popcorn-like white waxy seeds. Confirm leaf-base glands and fruit whenever possible.
